newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal may create pulp holding with Arjo.
newsitem.headline: Portugal may create pulp holding with Arjo.

text.p: Portugal's government is studying creating a new holding company in the pulp and paper sector and could offer to Arjo Wiggins Appleton a smaller stake in the enlarged company in place of its 43.5 percent stake in Soporcel, a Lisbon newspaper reported.

Diario Economico said it had learned that the government was considering two scenarios for the restructuring of the sector, both of which contemplate the creation of a new holding controlled by the state.
Under one scenario, the Portuguese state would hold a majority stake in the holding firm in a transitory phase before privatising the company.

Portuguese bank Caixa Geral de Depositos and Arjo Wiggins Appleton, which together control state-owned pulp group Soporcel-Sociedade Portuguesa de Celulose, would take stakes of less than 25 and 30 percent respectively. Caixa's current stake in Soporcel is 50.5 percent.
In the second scenario, the new holding company would be controlled by state pulp group Portucel Industrial, with minority stakes of similar amounts held by Caixa and Arjo Wiggins.
Government officials were not immediately available to comment on the report.
